record.file_problem: GitHub README and file list only; code and result files were not read or run. The README reports findings and names result artifacts.
record.tranche_reason: The README reports a difference-in-means refusal direction and a subtraction steering test on Llama-3.2 models, using the direction method to test a causal refusal effect in new model and deployment settings.
record.gate_note: The README reports direction-cosine and behavioral results under INT4, an eager-versus-torch.compile comparison, and a Block 8 steering intervention with a random-direction control. Values used to choose settings and setup steps are not treated as results. The positive-control postmortem and PCA visualization descriptions are not recorded as rows because they do not report a refusal-behavior result or a result that tests a listed version.
record.test_reason: The study's only test of the claim is a causal one: subtracting the difference-in-means refusal direction at a single block (Block 8, alpha=5) on Llama-3.2-1B, with a random-direction control. This is a different intervention from the original's all-layer directional ablation, aimed at the same question. Its main focus, whether the direction survives INT4 quantization or torch.compile, measures direction stability (cosine) and refusal behaviour under quantization. That is a related construct, not a version of the claim.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The README concludes that INT4 shifts the 1B refusal direction beyond the noise floor and slightly raises genuine compliance (4 to 10 of 520). The 3B model is more robust, and torch.compile leaves cosines unchanged. Subtracting the direction at Block 8 induced 100% compliance, unlike a random-direction control. The authors flag limits: one model family, one layer, unscaled alpha, and no style-only control.
record.recipe_differences: The repository says it builds on Arditi et al. (2024)'s methodology. It reports a single-block subtraction steering test rather than removal at every layer and position, and also tests direction and behavior under INT4 and torch.compile. This is a pilot-study repository, not explicitly described as a replication.
record.method_sensitivity: Model size/layer differs: the 1B result is at Block 8 and the 3B result at Block 14. The 3B cosine is from a single split without a confidence interval. The steering intervention uses alpha=5, which was not scaled to residual-stream norm; no style-only control direction was implemented.

fits_no_version.finding: Under INT4 quantization the 1B Block-8 refusal direction shifts beyond the split-half noise floor (cos 0.916 vs 0.946). The 3B Block-14 direction is more stable (0.970 vs 0.988), and torch.compile gives identical cosines to eager mode.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The difference-in-means refusal direction is stable under deployment-time optimizations (quantization, compilation), more so in larger models.

fits_no_version.finding: INT4 quantization slightly raised genuine compliance on 1B (4 to 10 of 520 AdvBench prompts). Keyword-matched refusal on 3B was essentially unchanged (98.08% vs 97.88%).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Quantization modestly degrades refusal behaviour in small models, alongside the shift in the refusal direction.

record.problems: README-reported results only; no code or underlying result files were inspected. One model family, one layer per model, and one INT4 method. The 3B cosine is from a single split with no confidence interval. Manual review of keyword failures was unblinded and done by one person. The torch.compile comparison was not checked for silent graph-break fallbacks. Steering was tested at one alpha without residual-stream norm scaling and without a style-only control. No general-capability test is reported.
record.rows_left_out: No other separately quantified results bearing on the listed versions were reported in the README. The positive-control weight-noise result and PCA visualization descriptions were not extracted as rows because they do not report a refusal-behavior outcome or test a listed version.

untested.parts: Directional ablation at every layer and position; adding the direction to induce refusal on harmless prompts; preservation of general capabilities; any causal test on the 3B model or under INT4.
Entire version: no jailbreak or adversarial-training test.
Entire version: no comparison with multi-direction accounts.
Entire version: harm judgment and refusal are not separated.
Entire version: no cross-language, cross-variant or base-to-instruct transfer test.
Entire version: no variation in refusal training.

missing.what: Real-direction steered outputs and their coherence; any alpha sweep or dose-response results for the causal steering. The README reports only alpha=5.
Per-layer cosine values across all 16 layers of the 1B model. These are plotted, but no numbers are given in the README.

record.verdict_notes: The source is a pilot GitHub README only; the code and result files were not inspected. The study is not an original source. Rows r1-r4 and r7 were relinked to none because they measure direction stability or quantization effects on behaviour, not mediation of refusal by the direction. The positive-control weight-noise test validates the cosine metric and is correctly omitted as a row.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test projecting the direction out of every layer and position, adding the direction to induce refusal to harmless requests, or whether general capabilities are largely preserved.
No weight-edit or released-model abliteration result is reported.
No jailbreak suppression test or training against direction ablation is reported.
No test compares a single direction with an affine, cone, or multiple-direction account.
No separate measurement of harmfulness judgment and refusal decision is reported.
Reports results for two model sizes, but does not test transfer of a direction across languages, variants, or base-to-instruct models.
No comparison of refusal-training methods or training stages is reported.

rows.subject: Llama-3.2-1B
rows.operation_detail: Compare the INT4 direction with the FP16 baseline direction using cosine similarity; the README identifies the direction as Block 8.
rows.measure: Bootstrapped cosine similarity of refusal directions
rows.note: The README says the INT4 direction is shifted beyond the sampling noise floor. This measurement alone does not establish the causal effect described by V1.
rows.check: Cosine stability of the direction under INT4 is a stability measure, not refusal mediation. It is recorded under fits_no_version.

rows.subject: Llama-3.2-3B

rows.uncertainty: not stated; README says this comes from a single split with no confidence interval
rows.note: The README describes the direction as more robust than in the 1B model. This is a direction-stability measurement, not a causal test of refusal mediation.
rows.check: Direction-stability cosine on the 3B model under INT4 (single split, no CI). It does not bear on V1's causal claim.

rows.subject: Llama-3.2-1B
rows.operation_detail: Evaluate genuine compliance on AdvBench after INT4 quantization, with manual adjustment for phrasing artifacts.
rows.note: This is a behavior result under quantization, not a direct ablation test of the direction.
rows.check: Change in refusal behaviour under quantization, with no direction intervention. This is not a test of mediation by the direction.

rows.subject: Llama-3.2-3B
rows.operation_detail: Compare keyword-matched refusal rates under FP16 and INT4.
rows.note: The README characterizes this as no detectable behavioral change. The prompt count for this 3B result is not stated.

rows.subject: Llama-3.2-1B
rows.operation_detail: Subtract the refusal direction at Block 8 with alpha=5.
rows.note: This is a single-block subtraction steering test, not projection out of every layer and position.

The README implies an unsteered FP16 1B model refuses nearly all AdvBench prompts (4/520 genuine compliance), but on a different prompt set (520 vs 100). The precision of the steered model is not stated. No coherence or capability check of the steered outputs is reported.

rows.subject: Llama-3.2 models
rows.size_stated: 1B and 3B, exact model-by-model results not stated

relationships.condition: Llama-3.2-1B, subtraction at Block 8 only, alpha=5 (not norm-scaled), 100 AdvBench prompts
relationships.reason: Subtracting the refusal direction gave 100% compliance, versus 12.2% mostly incoherent non-refusal for a random direction (r5, r6). No capability check was reported.
relationships.display_finding: Direction subtraction produced 100% compliance across 100 AdvBench prompts, versus 12.2% mostly incoherent non-refusal from random-direction steering.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Llama-3.2-1B, Block 8 subtraction, alpha=5, 100 AdvBench prompts
reader_labels.reason: Subtraction of the refusal direction yielded 100% compliance, while the random-direction control produced only a 12.2% non-refusal rate, largely from incoherent output (r5–r6). This supports a causal effect in this tested setting, not the full all-layer claim.
